### Autopilot-stack

The default autopilot: build a queue of PRs, verify each at its current head, stop at verified, and hand the PRs to the owner without merging. The main session runs every push, `gh` call, and `watch-pr` job; workers return patches and evidence. Merging is `skill://ulw/playbooks/autopilot-full.md`, and only when the owner explicitly asks for it.

1. **Fix the queue and the authority.** Write the queue (items, order, which PR builds on which) to `.omp/plans/<name>.md`. An autopilot request, or an unqualified "autopilot", means this playbook. It covers pushing branches and opening PRs for the named queue only, never a merge, and never an item the owner marked as theirs. If it is unclear whether PR creation was approved, ask once with the `ask` tool; a timed-out question is not a yes.
2. **Build with one worker per PR.** Each worker is an isolated `task` worker whose brief names the `skill://` files it must read, the done condition, and "return a patch, the proposed PR title and body in a file, and evidence; never push or run `gh`". Independent PRs run in parallel off trunk. The main session reads each patch, applies it, runs the repo's checks for the touched paths on the committed head, and only then pushes and opens the PR per `skill://ulw/playbooks/opening-a-pr.md`, early enough that CI and review bots run alongside the work.
3. **Stack a PR only when it builds on another PR.** This is the one exception to building off trunk. Base the PR on the other PR's branch, per Size and stacks in `skill://ulw/playbooks/opening-a-pr.md`. Each PR rebases onto its parent PR's branch and the stack root rebases onto trunk. A new head on a lower PR restacks the PRs above it, and a PR whose `git patch-id` (`git diff $(git merge-base <parent> <sha>) <sha> | git patch-id --stable`) the restack leaves unchanged keeps its verdict.
4. **Code-ready before self-proof.** The code is ready only after `skill://no-comments` and `skill://unslop` over the diff. Then rebase onto the parent branch (trunk for the root), record the code-ready head SHA in the queue file, and run the checks on that head, so verification runs on the base the patch lands on. Fix rounds stay on that base unless trunk conflicts, breaks CI, or lands a known change to the same files, because each rebase restarts CI.
5. **Verify once at the code-ready head.** A full `skill://swarm` runs once, at the code-ready head, and again only for new behavior, a redesign, or a large new diff. A rebase, a conflict resolution, or a minor fix gets one verifier at the new head, and a wording-only change gets none. Verifiers are separate workers that did not write the code (a different tier from the author where possible), re-run the gates, prove the load-bearing behavior on the real surface through the project's `verify-<app>` skill (`skill://verify`), and audit the diff. A verdict is bound to the head SHA and its patch-id in the queue file. Block only on a problem you can show with a failing run at the head or a doc line the PR made wrong. A follow-up is only for a problem the base already had; a defect in the PR's own diff is fixed in that PR (the same-pass rule in `agent/AGENTS.md`).
6. **Babysit to green, frontier first.** Run `skill://ulw/playbooks/babysit.md` in `drive` mode per stack: the main session runs `watch-pr` as a background bash job, fixes arrive as patches from workers, and the main session pushes each wave and replies to review threads citing the SHA. Never merge, even with every check green.
7. **In place of a merge, stop at verified.** Stop when each PR is verified and green (`watch-pr` exit 0 `READY`) at its current head, then hand the PRs to the owner. After the handoff nobody pushes, replies, or retargets without the owner's go. In a TUI main session, enter loop mode with the `loop` tool (`action: enter`, a `prompt` that names this file so each wake sees the no-merge rule, an `iterations` or `minutes` bound, and a `condition` command that exits 0 once every PR is verified and green). Where the `loop` tool is refused, the wake is the background `watch-pr` job's exit. Record base-already-had follow-ups in the queue file and do not fold them into a verified PR.

Reply. In Korean, plain text: each PR with its URL, base, head SHA, and verdict, what is green, what is parked as a follow-up, and that nothing is merged until the owner says so.
